A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniGraspTransformer and provide readable text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A-C. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulated grasping results, including its own success rates in Table 2, ablations, and quantitative grasp-diversity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a comparison against DAgger in Table 6.

M1.justification: The object-specific PPO teachers, offline trajectory distillation, Transformer architecture, inputs, rewards, and S-Encoder/V-Encoder training remain unchanged. The added DAgger experiment evaluates a comparator rather than modifying the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both retain the 3,200 training objects, 140 unseen objects from seen categories, 100 objects from unseen categories, state-based and vision-based tasks, and reported 12-object Inspire Hand deployment. The new comparison uses the existing 400-object evaluation scope.

E2.justification: DAgger with MLPs becomes an explicitly evaluated comparator in the 400-policy distillation experiment in v2 Table 6. The comparator set in the main benchmark, Table 2, remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds an online-versus-offline comparison design using 400 dedicated teachers and evaluation on the corresponding seen objects, comparing DAgger with MLPs against the Transformer. Existing pose splits, rollout lengths, success metrics, and training iteration counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds the targeted online-versus-offline distillation comparison. Existing scalability, input, encoder, reward, and diversity analyses remain. Consolidation of the qualitative comparison retains five of seven examples from v1 Figure 11, omitting two.

E5.justification: Evaluation repetitions, the diversity-analysis sampling procedure, and plotted ranges are retained. V2 adds no seed information, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 Table 6 newly reports DAgger at 88.2%, compared with the existing 400-object UniGraspTransformer result of 92.5%. Table 2 and the matched earlier ablation values remain unchanged. Two qualitative comparison examples are omitted.

T1.justification: The reward definitions, point-cloud transformations, encoder losses, and policy prediction objective are retained, including Equations 1-11. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about simplified distillation, scalability, generalization, and grasp diversity. The stated vision-based success-rate advantages also remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting offline distillation and larger networks to generalization and diversity retain their meaning. The new comparison paragraph reiterates this existing rationale; no substantive new applicability boundary or limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: Section 4 replaces the three-hours-per-policy description with parallel training of all 3,200 policies on 16 V100 GPUs in 80 hours. Appendix A.2 still states approximately three hours per policy on one V100, leaving the relationship between these timings unexplained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Dextrah-G, Grasp Anything, ArtiGrasp, and GraspXL and removes three earlier references. Section 2 slightly broadens its critique of prior approaches to include limited training-object coverage, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 tightens several methodological and related-work passages, adds the online-versus-offline paragraph, and introduces a supplementary-material heading. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 6, reformats Figure 4, and expands Figure 5 using five comparisons already present in v1 appendix Figure 11, removing that standalone figure and two examples. It also revises Figure 10's caption and adjusts table placement and spacing.

improvement.justification: The new DAgger comparison modestly strengthens evidence for the proposed design, while Figure 5 consolidates previously dispersed illustrations. The gain is limited: the comparison changes architecture and distillation together, and the revised training-time total remains unreconciled with Appendix A.2. The principal results and methodological documentation are preserved.
